name: Exact-Diagonalization Benchmark for Spectral Truncation in the Spinless Holstein Chain
description: We construct a reproducible finite-system exact-diagonalization benchmark designed to distinguish spectral truncation by transition weight from truncation by excitation energy in the local zero- temperature Green function of the one-dimensional spinless Holstein chain. The purpose is to provide a finite-system spectral reference against which Green-function truncations can be tested, while keeping exact Lehmann transitions conceptually separate from operator-space basis elements. We study open chains at half filling for t= 1, g= 0.5, ω0 = 1, and µ= 0, with an explicitly imposed local phonon cutoff nmax = 1. The relevant N, N−1, and N + 1 particle-number sectors are completely diagonalized for L = 2,4,6, with full truncated Fock-space dimensions 16, 256, and 4096. The ground-state energies are−1.1506801239,−2.5362390322, and−3.9427406059, respectively. Using a transition-weight resolution threshold of 10−8, the calculations resolve 8, 75, and 259 Lehmann transitions, with cumulative resolved weights 1.0000000000, 0.9999999337, and 0.9999995360. A separate phonon-cutoff study shows that the nmax = 1 ground-state energies are not converged with respect to the phonon Hilbert space. The production results are therefore exact for the explicitly specified finite truncated Hamiltonians, not for the infinite-phonon model. We also document an L = 8 sparse-sector diagnostic, but do not interpret it as a complete spectral calculation.
